scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: In the late 1800s the street was a "riot of ornament" along which around 150 retail shops plied their trade, many with wrought iron decorating the outsides of their buildings.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: Mayor Hercules Jarvis named it Adderley Street in 1850, to honour British Parliamentarian Charles Bowyer Adderley (elevated to the peerage as Baron Norton in 1878) who fought successfully against the plan for the British…

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: The network of canals were covered over, throughout Cape Town, in the 1860s.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: It also has long been a financial centre with the Colonial Bank located on the site of the Stuttafords Building until 1890, and the imposing Standard Bank Building on the east side at Hout Street.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: Adderley Street is home to numerous office buildings, including Foreshore Place (formerly ABSA Centre), which was completed in 1970, and is currently Cape Town's 6th tallest building.

scenes.title: The place
scenes.text: A supply station founded in 1652 by the Dutch East India Company at the foot of Table Mountain. Adderley Street, the commercial artery of the colonial town, saw trams and markets at the turn of the 20th century.
